mission:
Add two independent utilities to this library, each with unit tests:
1. In src/math.js add `clamp(value, min, max)` which returns value limited to the inclusive range and throws a RangeError when min > max. Add tests to test/math.test.js.
2. In src/strings.js add `slugify(text)` which lowercases, trims, replaces runs of non-alphanumeric characters with a single hyphen and strips leading/trailing hyphens. Add tests to test/strings.test.js.
The two utilities touch different files and must be implemented as separate parallel tasks. `npm test` must pass with no regressions.

plan.summary: Add two independent named exports to the ESM utility library: `clamp(value, min, max)` in src/math.js and `slugify(text)` in src/strings.js, each with node:test unit tests in the matching existing test file. The repo is tiny (package.json sets "type": "module" and "test": "node --test"; src/math.js currently exports only `add`, src/strings.js only `capitalize`; each test file has one one-line test using node:assert/strict). The two changes touch disjoint files, so they are planned as two parallel worker tasks with no dependency between them; each task runs `npm test` itself to verify.
assumptions: clamp's bounds are inclusive: value equal to min or max is returned unchanged; when min === max that value is returned and no error is thrown.
clamp does no type validation or NaN handling beyond the requested RangeError for min > max (not specified in the request).

slugify treats 'alphanumeric' as ASCII a-z and 0-9 after lowercasing; any other character (whitespace, punctuation, underscores, accented/non-ASCII letters) is part of a run replaced by a single hyphen.
slugify of an empty string or a string with no alphanumeric characters returns an empty string; no input type validation is added.
No README update is required; the request only asks for the functions and tests.
Code style follows the existing files: ESM named `export function`, 2-space indent, no semicolons, single quotes, no comments.
acceptanceCriteria: src/math.js exports `clamp(value, min, max)` returning value limited to the inclusive [min, max] range and throwing RangeError when min > max; existing `add` export is unchanged.

src/strings.js exports `slugify(text)` that lowercases, trims, replaces runs of non-alphanumeric characters with a single hyphen and strips leading/trailing hyphens; existing `capitalize` export is unchanged.
test/math.test.js contains tests for clamp and test/strings.test.js contains tests for slugify, alongside the untouched existing `add` and `capitalize` tests.
`npm test` (node --test) exits 0 with all tests passing, including the pre-existing `add` and `capitalize` tests.
Only src/math.js, src/strings.js, test/math.test.js and test/strings.test.js are modified; no new files or dependencies are added.

tasks.title: Add clamp(value, min, max) to src/math.js with unit tests
tasks.description:
In the ESM library (package.json has "type": "module", test script is `node --test`), add a named export `clamp(value, min, max)` to src/math.js, below the existing `add` function. Behaviour: if min > max throw a `RangeError` (with a short descriptive message); otherwise return value limited to the inclusive range [min, max] (min if value < min, max if value > max, else value). Do not change `add`. Match existing style: `export function`, 2-space indent, no semicolons, single quotes, no comments.

Then add tests to test/math.test.js, which already imports `test` from 'node:test', `assert` from 'node:assert/strict' and `{ add }` from '../src/math.js'. Extend the import to include `clamp`, keep the existing `add` test untouched, and add tests covering: value inside the range is returned unchanged; value below min returns min; value above max returns max; value equal to min and equal to max is returned (inclusive bounds); min === max works; min > max throws RangeError (use `assert.throws(() => clamp(1, 5, 2), RangeError)`).

Only touch src/math.js and test/math.test.js; another agent is editing src/strings.js and test/strings.test.js in parallel. Run `npm test` from the repository root and confirm it exits 0. Do not add dependencies or create other files.
acceptanceCriteria: src/math.js has a named export `clamp` and the existing `add` export is unchanged.
clamp(1, 5, 2) throws an error that is an instance of RangeError.
test/math.test.js contains clamp tests covering in-range, below-min, above-max, boundary values and the RangeError case, and still contains the original `add` test.
`npm test` exits 0 with no failing tests.
Only src/math.js and test/math.test.js are modified by this task.

tasks.title: Add slugify(text) to src/strings.js with unit tests
tasks.description:
In the ESM library (package.json has "type": "module", test script is `node --test`), add a named export `slugify(text)` to src/strings.js, below the existing `capitalize` function. Behaviour: lowercase the text, trim it, replace every run of one or more non-alphanumeric characters (anything other than a-z and 0-9 after lowercasing) with a single hyphen, then strip any leading and trailing hyphens. An empty string or a string with no alphanumeric characters yields ''. Do not change `capitalize`. Match existing style: `export function`, 2-space indent, no semicolons, single quotes, no comments.

Then add tests to test/strings.test.js, which already imports `test` from 'node:test', `assert` from 'node:assert/strict' and `{ capitalize }` from '../src/strings.js'. Extend the import to include `slugify`, keep the existing `capitalize` test untouched, and add tests covering: lowercasing and space replacement ('Hello World' -> 'hello-world'); surrounding whitespace trimmed ('  Hello World  ' -> 'hello-world'); a run of mixed non-alphanumerics collapses to one hyphen ('foo -- _bar!!baz' -> 'foo-bar-baz'); leading/trailing non-alphanumerics are stripped ('--Hello, World!--' -> 'hello-world'); digits are preserved ('Node 20 LTS' -> 'node-20-lts'); empty and symbol-only input return '' ('' -> '', '!!!' -> '').

Only touch src/strings.js and test/strings.test.js; another agent is editing src/math.js and test/math.test.js in parallel. Run `npm test` from the repository root and confirm it exits 0. Do not add dependencies or create other files.
acceptanceCriteria: src/strings.js has a named export `slugify` and the existing `capitalize` export is unchanged.
slugify('Hello World') === 'hello-world' and slugify('  Hello World  ') === 'hello-world'.

test/strings.test.js contains slugify tests covering lowercasing, trimming, run collapsing, leading/trailing hyphen stripping and empty/symbol-only input, and still contains the original `capitalize` test.
`npm test` exits 0 with no failing tests.
Only src/strings.js and test/strings.test.js are modified by this task.

risks.description: The request does not define 'alphanumeric' for slugify; a Unicode-aware implementation would keep accented letters while an ASCII one turns them into hyphens, so implementation and tests could disagree with the requester's intent.
risks.mitigation: The plan fixes the ASCII interpretation (a-z, 0-9 after lowercasing) as a stated assumption and the task's tests use ASCII-only inputs, so the behaviour is unambiguous and easy to widen later.

risks.description: Each parallel task runs `npm test`, which executes both test files; a task may see a transient failure caused by the other task's in-progress edits if they share a working tree.
risks.mitigation: The tasks touch disjoint files and neither imports the other's module; if a failure originates in the other task's files, re-run after it completes, and rely on the final mission-level `npm test` run on the merged result.

risks.description: A worker could accidentally alter or replace the existing `add` / `capitalize` functions or their tests while editing the same files, causing a regression.
risks.mitigation: Each task explicitly instructs appending below the existing code and keeping existing tests untouched, with acceptance criteria requiring the original exports and tests to remain and `npm test` to pass.

approvals.command:
cat >> src/strings.js <<'EOF'

export function slugify(text) {
  return text
    .toLowerCase()
    .trim()
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-')
    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '')
}
EOF
sed -i "s/{ capitalize }/{ capitalize, slugify }/" test/strings.test.js
cat >> test/strings.test.js <<'EOF'
test('slugify lowercases and replaces spaces', () => assert.equal(slugify('Hello World'), 'hello-world'))
test('slugify trims whitespace', () => assert.equal(slugify('  Hello World  '), 'hello-world'))
test('slugify collapses runs of non-alphanumerics', () => assert.equal(slugify('foo -- _bar!!baz'), 'foo-bar-baz'))
test('slugify strips leading and trailing hyphens', () => assert.equal(slugify('--Hello, World!--'), 'hello-world'))
test('slugify preserves digits', () => assert.equal(slugify('Node 20 LTS'), 'node-20-lts'))
test('slugify returns empty string for empty input', () => assert.equal(slugify(''), ''))
test('slugify returns empty string for symbol-only input', () => assert.equal(slugify('!!!'), ''))
EOF
